title:
La ci darem la mano
 La la lala la la.
html_source:
From Don Giovanni (opera) by Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart

“There we will be hand in hand”

This is the first line of Don Giovanni’s attempt to seduce Zerlina, who is betrothed to Masetto. It is an especially poignant feature of Bloom’s mental wandering as it layers distinct memories and infidelities.

Firstly, it refers back to the conversation that Bloom and Molly have in the morning, after she has received a letter from her lover/manager, Blazes Boylan.

– Who was the letter from? he asked.
Bold hand. Marion.
– O, Boylan, she said. He’s bringing the programme.
– What are you singing?
– La ci darem with J. C. Doyle, she said, and Love’s Old Sweet Song.

Moreover, this bit of song stuck in Bloom’s head precedes his reading of the letter from Martha, his lover-by-correspondence.

The biggest irony, however, is that the context for why the song is stuck in his head in the first place has to do with the connection that Bloom has to his wife and his longing to be restored fully as her principal love and partner. As cheeky as it is to think of Bloom as the Don Giovanni to his numerous half-mistresses, the request for union, of being “hand in hand” with his wife again provides the ironic pathos of this unconsciousness.
